parties:
Hubble Corporate Ltd  ------ Petitioners
 Vs.
Artha Rin Adalat & others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
The petitioner, Hubble Corporate Limited is a private limited company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1913. In course of its business, the petitioner imported some water pumps from Italy through Letter of Credit (L/C) No. IMD/46/SEMR/162 dated 2-5-1996. The L/C was opened through the respondent No.2 Rupali Bank Limited, Ibrahim Mansion Corporate Branch, Purana Paitan, Dhaka (hereinafter referred to as the Bank). The value of the said L/C was US$ 107565.78. The imported water pumps were initially stored at the Bank's godown at the request of the petitioner. When the imported water pumps were lying in the Bank's godown at Mirpur, Dhaka, due to rainwater leaking through the godown premises, the goods started decorating. The petitioner informed the matter to the Bank and asked to shift the goods immediately but the Bank did not shift the goods from the said godown as a result of which the entire goods were damaged due to the devising flood of 1998. As a custodian of the goods the Bank's duty was to take care of the goods. The goods of the petitioner were damaged due to negligence of the Bank. The Bank, as a bailey was under legal obligation to protect the goods of the petitioner under section 151 for the Contract Act. Therefore, the Bank is liable to pay compensation for the damaged of the imported goods of the petitioner. So the petitioner filed Money Suit No. 42 of2004 against the Bank before the 5th Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka (herein after stated as the Court) for compensation of an amount of Taka 59,38,897. The goods were covered under the insurance policy with other the goods belonged to other clients of the Bank. But the Bank ultimately accepted the claim for only a sum of Taka 15,000 offered by the Insurance Company although the petitioner rejected the said offer by its letter dated 19-6-2003 and 4-8-2003. By accepting the said amount the Bank has waived all claim against the petitioner and there was no cause of action against the petitioner. But the Bank filed Artha Rin Suit No. 182 of 2005 against the petitioner and the proforma respondent No. 4 before the Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka (Shortly, the Adalat) for recovery of loan amounting to Taka 86,35,438.65 as on 31-3-2005. The petitioner appeared in that suit and filed an application for rejection the plaint under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure (in short, the Code) read with sections 46 and 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (the Ain, in short) stating that the suit is barred by limitation under section 46 of the Ain and that there was no cause of action for the suit. The learned Judge of the Adalat rejected the said application, which resulted in this writ petition. 

 4. Respondent No.2, the Bank contested the rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition as well as a supplementary affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter alia, that the suit was not barred by limitation under section 46 of the Ain; that the suit was filed within the period of limitation and there was proper cause of action for filing of the suit and the learned Judge of the Adalat in consideration of legal and factual questions involved in the case lawfully rejected the application on merit; whether the goods were damaged or not in a disputed question of fact; that the defendant-petitioner opened letter of credit with the Bank for import of low lift water pump and after receipt of shipping documents the Bank requested the petitioner to retire the imported goods against payment but the petitioner by letter dated 25-8-1996 prayed for LIM facilities expressing its inability to retire the goods and accordingly, the Bank allowed LIM facilities in favour of the petitioner and goods of the said L/C were shifted to the Bank's godown; that the petitioner had failed to take delivery of the  said goods on payment; that the petitioner claimed that their imported goods were damaged during the flood of 1998 and they requested the Bank to submit claim before the insurance authority; that the Bank forwarded the claim of the petitioner to the concern insurance company namely, the Central Insurance Company Limited; that by letter dated 28-7-2003 the insurance company informed the Bank that the goods of the petitioner were apparently found in sound condition which was communicated to the petitioner; that thereafter the petitioner by letter dated 20-5-2002 requested the Bank for waiver of interest, extension of time to make payment and for taking delivery of the goods; that considering the said letter, the Bank by letter dated 21-8-2002 and 9- 9-2002 allowed the petitioner some time to repay the dues and the petitioner by letter dated 28-2-2002 accepted the terms and conditions of the Bank's offer and undertook to repay all the outstanding dues of the Bank; that subsequently the petitioner took delivery of the pledged and LIM goods on 25-3- 2009 from the Bank's godown; that the petitioner defaulted to liquidate the outstanding dues of the Bank in spite of repeated request and reminders though the petitioner wrote various letters to the Bank and undertook to repay the same'; that the Bank then served final notice upon the petitioner on 14-3-2004 for payment of the loan and after receiving the said final notice the petitioner served a legal notice demanding justice upon the Bank with some false story on 12-5-2004; that before receiving final notice on 14-3-2004 the petitioner never raised any objection against its loan liability and on each and every occasion the petitioner undertook to repay the outstanding liabilities of the Bank; that in this circumstances the Bank was compelled to file the Artha Rin Suit for recovery of outstanding loan lawfully and the impugned order was passed by the learned Judge of the Adalat in accordance with law and therefore, the rule is liable to be discharged, 

 6. Mr M Sakhawat Hossain, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, however, did not raise the question on limitation in filing of the suit in view of the provision of section 46 of the Ain inasmuch as the aforesaid question law has been settled in a good number of cases. He frankly concedes that the Artha Rin Suit No. 182 of 2005 is not barred by limitation. 

 (5) the suit was not barred by limitation and there was cause of action for suit; 

 14. Admittedly, the petitioner also repaid some loan from time to time to the Bank. It transpires from the Bank's final demand letter for recovery of loan (Anneure-3/1 to the supplementary affidavit- in-opposition) that it was sent to the petitioner on 14-3-2004. It further transpires from the petitioner's legal notice (page 40 of the supplementary affidavit) that it was issued on May 12,2004 claiming compensation alleging damage of goods at the Bank's godown, etc. The petitioner thereafter also filed a suit for compensation against the Bank. Therefore, it is evident that after receiving' the final notice from the Bank the petitioner first claimed compensation and then filed a suit. The learned Advocate for the petitioner admitted that the Bank's suit is not barred by limitation.
